thread:
lee.devex: FYI customer reported rerank break after upgrading Ruby SDK. Seems Ruby and Go disagree on streaming embeddings shape when batching-helper + auth-retry are involved.

lee.devex: repro: server streams two chunks; Go appends per-chunk vectors and validates against meta.pad_to=512; Ruby flattens and splits assuming a legacy "vector_count" header. Result: Ruby sometimes returns vectors length 511.

anya-ruby: we have a legacy shim for flattened unary responses. Streaming changed semantics and the shim mis-splits. Also seeing failures only when FORCE_AUTH_FLAP=true in sample-app -> suggests retry reassembly problem.

tom-go: Go app treats each chunk as list-of-vectors and checks per-vector length. We added that validator after a similar bug.

sasha-ml: likely two issues: (1) Ruby parser shim flattening, (2) retry/stream reassembly dropping a float at chunk boundary. Can reproduce locally with auth-flap.

ci-bot: Created issue #4123 assigned to @anya-ruby and @tom-go.

anya-ruby: plan: remove flattening shim, implement streaming parser that accepts chunked vectors, add per-vector pad_to assertion and retry-on-mismatch (2 attempts). Opening draft PR.

tom-go: I'll add cross-SDK CI integration test against a streaming mock that simulates auth-flap and random float split boundaries. Fail on any dim mismatch.

sasha-ml: runtime follow-up: include vectors_in_chunk and per-vector checksum in stream meta to avoid SDK guesswork.

lee.devex: customer workaround: use Go SDK or set sample-app to unary mode. ETA ~48h for Ruby SDK patch.

anya-ruby: adding telemetry event "embed.dim_mismatch" for visibility.

lee.devex: resolving thread for now, will reopen if regressions continue.
